newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bosnian refugee is Berlin hijacker say police.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian refugee is Berlin hijacker say police.

text.p: A knife-wielding Bosnian war refugee hijacked an Austrian Airlines plane bound for Vienna on Tuesday, but was disarmed by a police commando unit shortly after the aircraft returned to Berlin, police said.

The 39-year-old Bosnian broke into the cockpit and told the pilot he wanted a residency and work permit in Germany. The plane returned to Berlin and was brought to an isolated hangar, where negotiations were set to start.
"But it never got that far because a police special unit overpowered the assailant and quickly arrested him," said Ruediger Reiff, spokesman for Berlin's justice ministry.
There were no injuries, he said.
There were 28 passengers and five crew aboard the aircraft, a McDonnell-Douglas MD-80.

There were reports that the hijacker was pushed down the steps of the plane, but that could not be immediately confirmed. Police said the hijacking was ended within about two minutes of the plane's coming to a halt.
Walter Bock, a chief pilot for Austrian Airlines in Vienna, said he was in radio contact with the plane and that the aircraft was nearly at its destination when the hijacker entered the cockpit.
He said he was carrying a knife and a bat in his hand and demanded the plane be turned back to Berlin, which is about 900 miles north of Vienna.
Reiff said the plane had left Berlin's Tegel airport at 11.20 a.m. and returned at 12.48 p.m.
Reiff said the Bosnian, who was only identified with the initial L., was facing immiment deportation from Germany.
There are some 320,000 Bosnian war refugees living in Germany. Several German states have recently begun the forced repatration of Bosnians to their home country.
The hijacker was charged with kidnapping and air piracy, police said.
